speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with a generalized rash; to begin my assessment, is your baby male or female, and how many days old are they?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the mother's history of gonorrhea and your baby's 4-day age, are there any pus-filled blisters (pustules) on the rash, and has the baby had any difficulty feeding or breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Infection. The clinical presentation of pustules on an erythematous base, sparing the palms and soles, in a 4-day-old infant with a maternal history of gonorrhea is classic for this diagnosis.
